profile.headline: Senior Principal Software Engineer at Berkshire Grey
profile.summary: Senior Principal Software Engineer managing the Perception and AI team for robotic picking. I wear two hats: driving the technical roadmap and managing the engineers who execute on it. My expertise in classical and learning-based perception allows me to bridge the gap between on-site field requirements and multi-month development roadmaps. I am adept at deciding what problems we need to solve, designing the technical architecture to solve them, and prioritizing our execution. I focus heavily on delivering highly reliable applications, because for us, bugs cause real-world bottlenecks and false positives cost time. At the end of the day, my job is to get the best out of high-performing engineers and ensure our robotic systems work flawlessly in the wild.

positions.title: Senior Principal Software Engineer | Robotic Pick Cells Perception/AI Team Lead and Manager
Principal Software Engineer | Robotic Pick Cells Perception/AI Team Lead and Manager
Software Engineer (Perception/AI)
positions.description: At Berkshire Grey, we believe it’s time to radically change the essential way we do business. Our game-changing solutions combine AI and Robotics to automate omni-channel fulfillment for enterprises serving today’s connected consumers. By transforming pick, pack and sort operations, our technology is a fundamental engine of change that moves you forward. Berkshire Grey customers include Global 100 retailers and logistics service providers.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Conducted research on rapid vision-based autonomous navigation for drones under Professor Camillo J. Taylor 
• Designed convolutional neural network to predict collisions using five consecutive first-person-view images
• Created 7 datasets of thousands of simulated drone collisions in various environments with AirSim and Unreal Engine

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern - Advanced Active Safety
positions.description:
• Collaborated on scrum team of 8 software developers and participated in daily stand-up and sprint planning meetings
• Developed algorithm for detection of objects left behind in a vehicle using two interior cameras
• Presented work to Product Owner and three scrum teams to propose implementation

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern - Robotics
positions.description:
• Proposed sensor and software architecture for KLM's mobile robot, Care-E, which produced over $50M for the company
• Programmed Care-E in team of 2 using ROS navigation stack and SLAM, and designed person following algorithm
• Consulted with multiple clients to establish electronic and software design for their projects

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
• Leveraged YOLO convolutional neural network and OpenCV to detect traffic signals and their status with 93% accuracy
• Build dataset of signals from scratch, combining web scraping, self-taken images, and data augmentation
• Integrated network in ROS to run system for all six cameras simultaneously

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Modulated controller for quadcopter stability during flight
• Simulated and implemented corridor navigation algorithm for quadrotor drone using V-REP software and Hokuyo LIDAR

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
• Worked on research project for realizing full human motion tracking for data analysis
• Learned to use ROS and developed URDF model of human to be be shown in rviz
• Integrated and filtered data from multiple IMU’s in ROS to articulate human model

company.name: MIT d’Arbeloff Laboratory for Information Systems and Technology

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Worked on converting Robotis Bioloid Humanoid into a “transformer” capable of changing into an automobile
• Learned RoboPlus software to control motors which actuated robot transformation process
• Gained proficiency in CAD to design 3D printed parts for robot exterior

company.name: New York City College of Technology Robotics Lab

educations.fieldOfStudy: Mechanical Engineering: Control, AI, and Robotics

courses.name: Analysis and Design of Feedback Control Systems

projects.title: Focused Semantic Edge Detection
projects.description:
• Combined and filtered three existing semantic segmentation datasets to create semantic edge detection datasets
• Trained Bi-Directional Cascade Network for Perceptual Edge Detection to only learn edges of image’s primary subjects

projects.title: Visual Question Answering Using Object Information as Metadata
projects.description:
• Explored methods to generate answers to VQA v2 dataset containing questions about images
• Created baseline model using ResNet-50 and logistic regression to generate answers
• Attained accuracy of 80% by modifying attention-based SOTA architecture to incorporate object location data
• Utilized AWS for all aspects of the project
